title: From Data Scarcity to Abundance? A Reproducible Benchmark of Quality-Gated Synthetic Data Pipelines for Tabular Model Training
description:
Synthetic data is often proposed for training models when real records are scarce or sensitive. Version 1 of this paper made quantitative claims about such pipelines with no experiment behind them, and this revision replaces those claims with a preregistered, reproducible benchmark. We describe a pipeline in which a planner chooses among candidate generators and a quality gate accepts a synthetic batch only if it stays close to a real holdout and is not closer to training records than fresh real records are. No language-model API was available. The planner is therefore a deterministic rule-based stand-in, and the language-model layer is still an untested design. We evaluate four local generators (Gaussian copula, class-conditional Gaussian mixture, SMOTE-style interpolation, independent marginals) and a memorising control on four public tabular datasets with five seeds. The gated pipeline retained between 96.1% and 99.6% of real-data test AUC. That supports the preregistered hypothesis of at least 90% retention, with no margin on credit-g, where the interval reached the threshold. Utility alone did not reveal leakage. Interpolation and copying kept near-real utility while membership-inference AUC rose as high as 0.82. The gate withheld every interpolation and copy release, and when the copier was tried first it lowered attack AUC to between 0.50 and 0.55. Under a simulated 30% fault rate, retry with fallback delivered 99.5% of requested rows (53420 of 53920). Adding synthetic rows to small real training sets gave no consistent gain.

Changes in version 2.0

  • New title, chosen to match the evidence. The LLM orchestration layer is now presented as an untested architecture, and a rule-based planner is measured in its place.
  • Removed every unmeasured claim of version 1: the 90-95% performance figure, the 60-80% cost reduction, the 6-18 month to 4-8 week timeline, the 40-60% LLM quality improvement, the three named case studies, and the claim that synthetic data eliminates privacy risk.
  • Added a preregistered benchmark on four public datasets with five generators and five seeds. Utility, fidelity, and privacy are measured on disjoint splits and reported with 95% intervals and a verdict file.
  • Added a fail-closed quality gate, calibrated on real data, that can abstain. Ablations switch the gate on and off and test an adversarial memorising generator, simulated generator faults, data scarcity, and missing data.
  • New Threats to Validity section. The regulatory-compliance mappings are gone, and every reference was corrected and checked against its DOI or arXiv record.
  • The code, cached data with checksums, results, tests, and the preregistration now ship together as a reproducible package.
notes: Reproduction: unzip synthetic-data-pipelines-v2-code-data.zip, create a Python 3.12 environment with numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn, matplotlib, and pytest, then run `python code/run_all.py` from the package root (about 8 minutes on an 8-core laptop CPU; cached data are included). `python code/run_all.py --analyze` rebuilds summaries, figures, and tables from results/. Tests: `python -m pytest tests`. Build the paper in paper/ with pdflatex and bibtex. The linked GitHub repository holds the version 1 code; the version 2.0 code, data, and results are in this Zenodo package.
